summary: Chamath makes the bull case for OpenAI at a $500B valuation by projecting DAU growth to 2B and applying a fraction of Facebook/Google ARPU, arriving at a ~$1.5T terminal valuation.
quote: if you take 400 or 500 million MAO DAO growing at... 50%... 500 goes to a billion, billion goes to 2 in 4 years. And at 2 billion DAO, they generate a 10th of Facebook's revenue... you probably get to a trillion 5 valuation there.

summary: Sacks argues OpenAI's dominant consumer position and real subscription revenue — plus its role as a search replacement — make a $500B valuation supportable on fundamentals.
quote: OpenAI has actual revenue... they have subscriptions and they appear to have the dominant position in the consumer space. And it is a replacement for a lot of people for search, which is the most lucrative franchise on the internet.

summary: Sacks views Meta's AI hiring freeze as a normal consolidation after aggressive acquihires rather than a sign of a broader bust, and does not make a directional investment call.
quote: I think that what Meta is doing is probably digesting a little bit. They've now made a bunch of talent acquisitions... and they're probably just consolidating a little bit.
